chapter: Clarinet teachers and the Baton Rouge scene
title: Knowing New Orleans music; slipping into dances
summary: Joe knew great musicians came from New Orleans; his father loved the French Opera, and Joe sneaked into Bernard Hall dances, meeting Buddy Petit at 14 or 15.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Were you ever made aware that there was any music like that in the rest of the country, or did you think it was something that came from where you lived, or...? Well, let me put it another way. Did you know, where you lived in Baton Rouge, that there was a hell of a movement of Jazz musicians and whatnot in New Orleans at that time, or didn't it occur to you, or what?

Well, I certainly knew great musicians came out of New Orleans. My Dad used to talk about the old French Opera in New Orleans, when great musicians came from France to play at the French Opera. The French Opera, unfortunately, burned down, I think, in early maybe 1912... Papa used to go there maybe once a month to see the opera.
Your Daddy, did he go to see these bands... Did he go dance with your mother and that kind of stuff?
Did you go by yourself or did you take...

Oh, I'd go with my brother or my sisters, or some of my cousins. When the Catholics gave a dance, the whole family would go. Papa never really was in for anything like that. Neither was my mother, because my mother was sick most all her life. But they wasn't people that went out at night like that. Now, when they had dances at Bernard Hall, we used to kind of slip in there. We wasn't allowed in there, you see. But we'd ease in there. But Manuel would get me in there, or sometimes Fritz, or... In fact, when I first met Buddy Petit, I must have been 14 or 15 years old, because I could play pretty good.
